scope: HodgeCY II related work for source-aware fidelity, double-octic refinement, Hilbert-Burch block explanation, and conservative novelty framing.

items.title: Complete classification of reflexive polyhedra in four dimensions
items.journal_or_publisher: Advances in Theoretical and Mathematical Physics
checked_claims: The four-dimensional reflexive-polytope classification contains 473,800,776 polytopes.
The same dataset has 30,108 distinct Hodge-number pairs.
This is historical context for many-to-one collapse at the Hodge-number level.
items.hodgecy_ii_relevance: This is the classical large-scale toric-hypersurface backdrop. HodgeCY II does not claim to discover Hodge-number degeneracy; it uses that phenomenon as motivation for finer source-aware fidelity layers.

items.title: Calabi-Yau Three-folds: Poincare Polynomials and Fractals
items.journal_or_publisher: Strings, Gauge Fields, and the Geometry Behind: The Legacy of Maximilian Kreuzer, World Scientific
checked_claims: The work studies statistical and fractal structure in Calabi-Yau data.
It reports 15,067,026 self-mirror entries in the Kreuzer-Skarke distribution.
It gives large same-Hodge multiplicities, including 910,113 for the pair (27,27), 877,191 for (25,25), and 875,275 for (26,26).
items.hodgecy_ii_relevance: This directly blocks any novelty claim of the form 'no previous work found 10,000+ Calabi-Yau collisions' when collision means repeated Hodge data or similarly coarse numerical data.

items.authors: Slawomir Cynk and Duco van Straten
items.title: Picard-Fuchs operators for octic arrangements I. The case of orphans
items.journal_or_publisher: Communications in Number Theory and Physics
checked_claims: The paper studies Picard-Fuchs operators for double octic arrangements.
Its abstract records 25 families in the orphan case, with seven order-two and eighteen order-four operators.
It emphasizes that Picard-Fuchs or birational-period data can separate families not distinguished by coarse Hodge information.
items.hodgecy_ii_relevance: This is the closest double-octic precedent for refining coarse Hodge information by more sensitive structure. HodgeCY II differs by tracking source assembly, rational/integral lattice data, equivariance, and later block-evaluation layers.

items.authors: Thomas W. Grimm, Fabian Ruehle, and Damian van de Heisteeg
items.title: Classifying Calabi-Yau Threefolds Using Infinite Distance Limits
checked_claims: The paper classifies infinite-distance limits in Kahler moduli space using limiting mixed Hodge structures.
It packages degeneration data in Hasse diagrams and reads off fibration information.
It treats examples from toric hypersurfaces and complete intersections in products of projective spaces.
items.hodgecy_ii_relevance: This is conceptual adjacency: degeneration-sensitive Hodge-theoretic structure refines ordinary topological/Hodge information. HodgeCY II does not identify its source assemblies or Hodge atoms with their LMHS invariants.

items.authors: Callum R. Brodie, Andrei Constantin, Andre Lukas, and Fabian Ruehle
items.title: Geodesics in the extended Kahler cone of Calabi-Yau threefolds
checked_claims: The paper studies extended Kahler/effective cones for h11=2 Calabi-Yau threefolds drawn from CICY and Kreuzer-Skarke constructions.
It compares topology-changing phenomena including flops and boundary behavior.
It is relevant as systematic cross-construction comparison, not as a HodgeCY source-fidelity census.
items.hodgecy_ii_relevance: This provides adjacent precedent for comparing Calabi-Yau data across construction frameworks. HodgeCY II's hierarchy is different: it is source/arrangement-aware and tracks first separation across rational, integral, equivariant, and geometric-evaluation layers.

items.authors: Aditi Chandra, Andrei Constantin, Cristofero S. Fraser-Taliente, Thomas R. Harvey, and Andre Lukas
items.title: Enumerating Calabi-Yau Manifolds: Placing Bounds on the Number of Diffeomorphism Classes in the Kreuzer-Skarke List
checked_claims: The paper uses Hodge numbers, triple-intersection data, second Chern class data, and integral basis changes/equivalence checks to bound diffeomorphism classes.
It relies on the Wall-Jupp classification framework for simply connected smooth Calabi-Yau threefolds with torsion-free cohomology.
It gives strong adjacent precedent for coarse collapse followed by finer integral/topological separation.
items.hodgecy_ii_relevance: This is especially important adjacent work. HodgeCY II should be framed as a different refinement ladder: local and Hodge data, rational source assembly, integral source lattice, equivariant structure, and verified geometric relation/evaluation layers.

items.authors: Anthony V. Geramita, Brian Harbourne, and Juan Migliore
items.title: Star configurations in P^n
checked_claims: Definition 2.1 imposes the properly-meeting condition on the hyperplanes.
Proposition 2.9 gives ACM status, h-vector, degree, and generator degree for star configurations under those hypotheses.
Proposition 2.6 supplies the basic-double-link construction used in the direct codimension-two proof below.
items.hodgecy_ii_relevance: The full properly-meeting theorem is stronger than the verified 84/84a hypotheses because higher-order point concurrences are allowed. HodgeCY II therefore uses the paper as standard context and uses the basic-double-link framework plus an explicit Hilbert-Burch matrix rather than citing Proposition 2.9 as a black box.

items.title: On ideals of finite homological dimension in local rings
items.journal_or_publisher: Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society
checked_claims: This is a primary source in the Hilbert-Burch tradition.
HodgeCY II uses the standard Hilbert-Burch theorem for perfect height-two ideals generated by maximal minors of an s by s-1 matrix.
items.hodgecy_ii_relevance: The Hilbert-Burch theorem explains the rank-seven syzygy package for the eight sevenfold-product generators.

items.title: Cohen-Macaulay Rings
checked_claims: Theorem 1.4.17 is a standard Hilbert-Burch reference.
items.hodgecy_ii_relevance: Used as a standard reference for the Hilbert-Burch theorem.

items.title: Commutative Algebra with a View Toward Algebraic Geometry
checked_claims: Theorem 20.15 is a standard Hilbert-Burch reference.
items.hodgecy_ii_relevance: Used as a standard reference for the Hilbert-Burch theorem and the determinantal resolution viewpoint.

novelty_statement.rejected_claim: No previous work has found >10,000 Calabi-Yau collisions.
novelty_statement.reason_rejected: Large degeneracies under Hodge numbers and other coarse invariants are already documented in the Kreuzer-Skarke distribution and later statistical studies.
novelty_statement.conservative_claim: Large degeneracies of Calabi-Yau data under Hodge numbers and other coarse invariants are well known, and previous work has refined them using intersection data, Chern classes, Picard-Fuchs operators, degeneration data, and integral topological invariants. What appears absent in the literature reviewed here is a source-aware computational fidelity census that records where presentations first separate along a hierarchy of local, Hodge, rational source-assembly, integral source-lattice, equivariant, and later geometric relation/evaluation invariants.

hodgecy_ii_story: A source-aware fidelity hierarchy for double-octic presentations.
A witness pair 84/84a that collapses at local, Hodge, and rational source levels but separates integrally.
An exact geometric continuation to verified 112-point block schemes.
A proved structural explanation showing why the block Hilbert/evaluation data collapse again.
A concrete non-monotone fidelity phenomenon: coarse equality -> integral source separation -> structurally forced block-evaluation collapse.
